operationalization: Classify documented internally viviparous species by respiratory organ and test whether any lacks aerial respiration; one verified counterexample refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive and respiratory traits of fishes

obstacles: Internal viviparity and air breathing require consistent definitions across taxa.
rationale: Both traits are standard zoological characters and broad comparative resources exist. Coverage is imperfect for invertebrates and unusual fishes, but the universal can be decisively refuted by a documented counterexample.

operationalization: Define hotness as measured core body temperature or metabolic rate, then compare lung-bearing and lungless species and lung vascularity classes with phylogeny and ambient temperature controlled.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database

obstacles: Aristotle's intrinsic heat is not identical to body temperature.
No single dataset joins lung anatomy and temperature across all animals.
rationale: A modern physiological proxy makes the comparison measurable, but substantial interpretation is unavoidable. Relevant measurements are scattered and taxonomically biased, allowing only a restricted comparative test.

operationalization: Use body temperature and water-balance physiology as proxies for heat and dryness, and model whether they predict oviparity and degree of egg development among birds and reptiles.

candidate_datasets.name: Amniote Life-History Database
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive mode and comparative life history

obstacles: Heat and dryness are underspecified causal essences.
Modern proxies do not uniquely represent Aristotle's mechanism.
rationale: The reproductive pattern is testable, but the proposed causes require contestable proxies. Existing comparative data could test associations, not uniquely discriminate this mechanism from phylogeny and alternative physiology.

operationalization: Map scolex to a larval stage and bloodless to absence of vertebrate blood, then inspect insect developmental modes and search larva-producing non-insects for counterexamples.

candidate_datasets.name: Catalogue of Life
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic backbone for the scoped groups

obstacles: Scolex does not map cleanly to one modern developmental category.
Developmental traits are not complete across insects.
rationale: The anatomical and developmental propositions have observable consequences. Public descriptions cover many groups, but testing every insect and the converse implication requires incomplete, harmonized trait data.

operationalization: Replace perfection with explicit developmental independence and heat with measured temperature or metabolic rate, then test whether reproductive modes occupy the asserted ordering.
obstacles: Perfection is evaluative rather than a standard variable.
The proposed linear ordering collapses diverse reproductive modes.
rationale: Parts of the reproductive sequence can be compared with modern traits, but the full claim embeds evaluative categories and an ambiguous heat scale. Existing data can resolve only a proxy version.

operationalization: For staged embryos, record the first detectable stage of each organ; differing onset stages confirm succession, while simultaneous presence from the earliest observable stage supports the rival.

candidate_datasets.name: eMouseAtlas
candidate_datasets.role: staged mouse embryo anatomy and imaging

obstacles: Detection thresholds differ among organs and imaging methods.
Full animal-wide scope exceeds model-organism coverage.
rationale: Organ onset is directly measurable in rich public developmental resources. Multiple model vertebrates provide a decisive test of succession, though not exhaustive coverage of all animals.

operationalization: Compare the first morphologically detectable heart and lung stages and their eventual sizes in staged embryos of lung-bearing vertebrates.

candidate_datasets.name: eMouseAtlas
candidate_datasets.role: staged heart and lung anatomy in mouse embryos

candidate_datasets.name: Human Developmental Biology Resource
candidate_datasets.role: human embryonic and fetal tissue resources and atlas data

obstacles: Appearance depends on the anatomical detection criterion.
Open staged imaging is concentrated in a few species.
rationale: The timing and size comparison is explicit and standard embryology atlases contain the required observations. The generalization is readily tested in representative mammals, with less complete taxonomic scope.

operationalization: Measure semen viscosity, opacity, colour and freezing state immediately after emission and across controlled cooling temperatures; each asserted transition has a direct refuting outcome.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Protein Atlas
candidate_datasets.role: public reproductive-tissue and protein context, though not cooling measurements

obstacles: Public raw cooling-series data on semen are scarce.
The claim combines several physical properties and broadens uncertainly beyond humans.
rationale: The experiment and criteria are straightforward, but existing open datasets rarely contain time-resolved physical measurements after cooling. Literature may resolve some components, so the claim is only partially resolvable without new data.

operationalization: Compile calibrated semen-colour measurements or clinical descriptions across human populations and animal species; any genuinely black sample under ordinary conditions refutes invariability.
obstacles: No known open population-scale semen-colour dataset.
Pathological and contaminated samples need prespecified handling.
rationale: Colour is directly observable and a counterexample would be decisive. Clinical literature likely bears on normal human semen, but broad population and animal coverage is not available as a coherent public dataset.

operationalization: Define general characters as conserved phylotypic structures and species-specific characters as derived diagnostic morphology, then compare their first appearance in staged embryos.
obstacles: General and species-peculiar characters require theory-dependent classification.
Cross-species stages are difficult to align.
rationale: Excellent developmental atlases exist, but the central categories are not directly observed and admit competing definitions. They permit informative tests in model species rather than a clean animal-wide resolution.

operationalization: No observation can identify a divine rational soul entering from outside independently of bodily activity.
obstacles: Divinity and entry from outside have no specified measurable consequence.
The claim denies a bodily correlate that data could track.
rationale: This is a metaphysical account rather than an operational biological proposition. No possible dataset distinguishes its central assertions from rivals.

operationalization: For cartilaginous fishes, record yolk depletion, uterine attachment and maternal nutrient transfer through gestation; placental attachment after yolk depletion confirms the claim in qualifying species.

candidate_datasets.name: Shark-References
candidate_datasets.role: public bibliography of shark and ray reproductive studies

obstacles: Detailed gestational anatomy is dispersed through species accounts.
The original taxonomic scope is imprecise.
rationale: Matrotrophy and placental viviparity are standard, observable elasmobranch traits. Existing species databases and literature can confirm or refute the claim for the intended smooth-hound examples.

operationalization: Convert each recorded menstruation onset to lunar phase and test whether onsets are enriched in the waning half relative to uniform timing, controlling cycle length and calendar effects.

candidate_datasets.name: Clue Research Dataset
candidate_datasets.role: large-scale menstrual-cycle research data access information

obstacles: App users are a selected population.
Repeated cycles per person and variable cycle lengths must be modeled.
rationale: The timing prediction and null distribution are clear, and large digital menstrual records exist for research. Existing analyses can discriminate a meaningful lunar enrichment, although access and sampling limit full population scope.

operationalization: Quantify morphology in reciprocal hybrid lineages over multiple backcrossed or intercrossed generations and test whether similarity shifts systematically toward the female line.
obstacles: The named crosses are rare, impossible, or poorly documented.
Multi-generation reciprocal pedigrees with morphology are not publicly assembled.
rationale: The directional prediction is testable with pedigreed hybrid data. Existing resources do not adequately cover the asserted crosses and successive generations, so a faithful test would require new breeding or systematic observations.

operationalization: Across staged vertebrate embryos, compare the first distinctly bounded heart stage with first appearance of every other organ; any earlier distinct organ refutes the universal.
obstacles: Distinctly formed is sensitive to imaging and anatomical definitions.
Model organisms cover a small fraction of vertebrates.
rationale: Developmental atlases make organ-order comparisons feasible and potentially decisive in several vertebrates. The universal scope and ambiguous threshold prevent complete resolution.

operationalization: Resolve erythrinus to candidate modern taxa and inspect sex records, gonadal anatomy and reproductive mode; one verified male refutes the observation.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish taxonomy, sex and reproductive biology

candidate_datasets.name: GBIF
candidate_datasets.role: specimen occurrence records for candidate taxa

obstacles: Erythrinus has uncertain modern taxonomic identity.
Most occurrence records omit sex and gonadal state.
rationale: Once a taxon is chosen, the claim has a decisive counterexample criterion and modern reproductive accounts can address it. Name ambiguity and sparse sex metadata restrict resolution.

operationalization: Examine sex differentiation, gonads and gamete production in Anguilla and candidate stagnant-water mullets; documented males or females refute sexlessness.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: sex and reproduction records for eels and mullets

candidate_datasets.name: FAO Fisheries and Aquaculture
candidate_datasets.role: species and aquaculture biology of eels and mullets

obstacles: The stagnant-water mullet is not securely identified.
Eel sex organs are inconspicuous outside maturation.
rationale: Modern fish biology directly documents differentiated sexes in eels, making the principal assertion resolvable and strongly falsifiable from existing evidence. The unidentified mullet component is less complete.

operationalization: Female-only reproduction can be observed, but the inference that males would otherwise be in vain and Nature makes nothing in vain supplies no independent measurable prediction.
obstacles: The final-cause premise is not empirically distinguishable.
Perfect generation is undefined.
rationale: Parthenogenesis can test a weakened factual statement, but not the claim's stated teleological necessity. No observation can establish that a sex exists for a non-vain natural purpose.

operationalization: Assign first-appearance stages and size classes to internal and external structures in embryo atlases, then test whether internal structures consistently precede external ones and large structures precede small ones.
obstacles: Internal versus external is ambiguous for early tissues.
Visibility depends on imaging resolution rather than formation alone.
rationale: Atlas data support direct timing tests in model organisms. The categories and universal scope introduce enough ambiguity that only a restricted version is presently resolvable.

operationalization: For mapped many-toed carnivores, code eye state and eyelid separation at birth; any normally open-eyed included species refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database

obstacles: Polydactylous is an ancient locomotor grouping, not modern polydactyly.
Neonatal eye-state fields are scattered among species accounts.
rationale: Birth eye state is an explicit, well-documented life-history trait in the named carnivores. Existing species accounts allow a practical counterexample search despite incomplete standardized coverage.

operationalization: Measure head, eye and hindlimb proportions through staged development and test whether relative head and eye size initially exceed later values while legs are initially smaller.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Developmental Biology Resource
candidate_datasets.role: human developmental imaging and tissue data

obstacles: The teleological explanation is not tested by the size pattern.
All-animal scope exceeds atlas coverage.
rationale: Public imaging permits quantitative tests of the morphological pattern in several vertebrates. It cannot distinguish the stated final-cause explanation, so the whole claim is only partially resolvable.

operationalization: Track relative eye volume and completion of ocular structures across staged embryos of terrestrial, aquatic and flying vertebrates, testing the claimed early enlargement, intervening collapse and late completion.

candidate_datasets.name: GEISHA
candidate_datasets.role: chicken embryo gene expression and developmental context

obstacles: Completion and collapse need explicit morphological definitions.
Comparable volumetric series are limited across taxa.
rationale: Developmental resources can test the sequence in representative vertebrates. The universal claim and the unusual collapse criterion are not covered consistently enough for full resolution.

operationalization: Compare ossification timing of the cranial vault with other bones, persistence of fontanelles after birth, and brain size or water content across humans and other mammals.
obstacles: Bregma is a landmark/fontanelle region rather than a single bone.
The causal brain-fluidity comparison lacks broad standardized data.
rationale: Ossification and postnatal fontanelle persistence are observable in imaging and anatomy sources. The causal explanation and claim of human maximality are much less directly covered.

operationalization: Model longitudinal skeletal growth and body size across age, and test whether cessation of bone growth temporally and mechanically constrains asymptotic body size.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: adult body size and life-history context

obstacles: Sets the limit is a causal claim with many endocrine and energetic confounders.
Longitudinal skeletal growth data are not broadly standardized.
rationale: Growth cessation can be measured, but identifying bone as the limiting cause rather than one component of coordinated growth is difficult. Existing datasets address patterns in subsets, not the universal mechanism.

operationalization: Measure marked hair shafts and follicle activity immediately before and after death, distinguishing true shaft elongation from skin dehydration and retraction.
obstacles: Public longitudinal postmortem hair measurements are scarce.
Apparent growth can result from skin shrinkage.
rationale: The claim has a clean physical test and strong discriminating criterion. Existing forensic literature can address it, but openly reusable raw datasets are limited, preventing a broad direct reanalysis.

operationalization: Classify tooth growth as continuous or determinate across toothed vertebrates and compare it with growth of other bones; any continuously growing non-dental bone or determinate teeth limits the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species accounts of dentition and growth

obstacles: Teeth are not bones in modern anatomy.
Continuous dental growth varies strongly among tooth types and taxa.
rationale: Comparative anatomy can directly resolve many examples and counterexamples. No single standardized trait matrix spans all bones and teeth across animals, and Aristotle's category mismatch complicates a full-scope verdict.

operationalization: Code erupted teeth or functional tooth analogues at birth or hatching across toothed animals and humans; any normally toothless nonhuman newborn refutes the universal.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database

obstacles: Tooth analogue and born require normalization across mammals and egg-layers.
Trait records are not complete for all animals.
rationale: The named human condition and many animal counterexamples are documented in public zoological sources. The universal is readily testable and refutable despite some category harmonization.

operationalization: Define nakedness as hair or feather coverage and scale nail or claw dimensions by body size, then rank humans among sampled animals.

candidate_datasets.name: Digital Morphology
candidate_datasets.role: comparative anatomy and measurable skeletal or keratinous structures

obstacles: Nakedness and nails are not homologous across all animals.
No broad open dataset standardizes nail size and body covering.
rationale: Explicit proxies make the superlatives testable, but the all-animal comparison is category-dependent and data-poor. Existing sources support selected comparisons rather than a comprehensive ranking.

operationalization: Count umbilical arteries and veins by species and regress total vessel count against adult or neonatal body size, testing the asserted one-two-many sequence.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: species body mass and life-history context

obstacles: Umbilical vessel counts are scattered in anatomy literature.
Adult size may not represent embryonic size at the measured stage.
rationale: Vessel count and body size are clear variables, but no single open comparative dataset joins them across placental mammals. A literature compilation can test a useful subset.

operationalization: Code upper-incisor presence, horns, uterine vasculature and placentome or cotyledon presence across viviparous quadrupeds, then test the stated conditional associations.
obstacles: Placental anatomy and uterine vasculature are not standardized in broad trait databases.
Ancient cotyledon terminology requires mapping to placentomes.
rationale: All characters are anatomically measurable and counterexamples are decisive. Data are dispersed across veterinary and comparative-anatomy literature, so existing resources resolve only a taxonomic subset.

operationalization: Measure placentome number and dimensions across gestational age in ruminants and test for monotonic shrinkage and disappearance by full fetal formation.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Veterinary Journal
candidate_datasets.role: public veterinary studies potentially containing ruminant gestational anatomy

obstacles: Longitudinal placentome measurements are scattered in papers.
Completion of the embryo needs a prespecified gestational criterion.
rationale: The anatomical trajectory is directly testable, and veterinary imaging studies can supply partial records. A harmonized open cross-species time series is not readily available.

operationalization: Compile fertility outcomes for F1 animal hybrids, distinguishing sex-specific sterility; any non-mule sterile hybrid refutes the universal.
obstacles: Hybrid fertility is rarely represented as a standardized public trait.
Sterility often differs between male and female hybrids.
rationale: The universal has clear counterexamples and can be assessed from existing biological literature. Public structured coverage of all relevant hybrids is incomplete, so a systematic analysis requires substantial compilation.

operationalization: No dataset can decide the normative methodological proposition that theories lacking subject-specific principles are empty.
obstacles: Empty is an epistemological evaluation, not a measurable outcome.
rationale: This is guidance about valid scientific reasoning. It does not assert a separable empirical pattern with confirming and refuting observations.

operationalization: Map domestic-ass occurrence and reproduction against minimum temperature and test whether established breeding populations are absent from cold climates.
obstacles: Domestic distributions are strongly shaped by human transport and husbandry.
Cold nature is not independently operationalized.
rationale: Modern occurrence and climate data can test the geographic and tolerance pattern. They cannot cleanly isolate intrinsic cold intolerance from husbandry and historical introduction, so the causal claim remains partial.

operationalization: Compare recorded conception and birth dates or gestation-length summaries for horses and asses with a 365-day prediction.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database

obstacles: One year may be an approximate ancient interval rather than exactly 365 days.
rationale: Gestation length is a standard, extensively documented variable for both named species. Existing data permit a direct and well-powered comparison with the asserted duration.

operationalization: Treat secretion coldness as measured semen temperature or metabolic activity and test whether horse-ass gamete mixing causes mule sterility through a temperature-dependent defect rather than chromosomal incompatibility.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Gene
candidate_datasets.role: genomic context for horse and ass reproductive incompatibility

obstacles: Cold secretion is not a defined modern mechanism.
Mule sterility has major chromosomal confounding.
rationale: Mule sterility itself is well known, but the proposed thermal mechanism lacks a faithful measurable variable in existing data. Modern genomic evidence bears indirectly on alternatives, not a clean reanalysis of Aristotle's causal model.

operationalization: Compile documented female-mule conceptions and outcomes, including live births, and compare reproductive physiology; one verified live birth refutes impossibility.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: public index of veterinary case reports on mule fertility

obstacles: Fertile female mules are rare, so evidence is case-report based.
Absence of menstrual secretion is not a standard equid variable.
rationale: The absolute birth prediction is readily refuted by documented cases, but data are sparse and distributed in veterinary reports. The stated physiological explanation is not directly represented in reusable datasets.

operationalization: Code internal egg formation, live birth, eggshell texture and egg colour across sharks and rays and test whether all scoped taxa share the asserted combination.
obstacles: Selachian reproductive modes are highly diverse.
Egg texture and colour are not standardized database fields.
rationale: Reproductive mode is well documented and makes much of the claim resolvable. The universal and detailed egg-character assertions require literature compilation beyond structured datasets.

operationalization: Across bird species, code production of unfertilised eggs, flight performance, predatory ecology and clutch size, then test for absence in raptors and association with weak flight and high fecundity.
obstacles: Unfertilised egg production is poorly standardized across wild birds.
Captive observations may not represent natural incidence.
rationale: The ecological associations are explicit, but the central wind-egg trait lacks broad public coverage. Existing data can test selected domestic and raptor comparisons only.

operationalization: Test whether relative investment in wings and feathers negatively predicts mating rate, gonadal investment and clutch size across birds after controlling body size, ecology and phylogeny.

candidate_datasets.name: AVONET
candidate_datasets.role: global bird morphology and ecological traits

obstacles: Residual matter is not measurable.
A correlation cannot uniquely establish resource diversion as the mechanism.
rationale: Modern allocation proxies and clutch data can test a restricted trade-off. Phylogeny, predation and flight ecology create serious confounding, and the Aristotelian material mechanism itself is not operational.

operationalization: For Cuculus canorus, compare clutch or annual egg number and documented nest placement with other birds; separate these observations from the unmeasurable cold-cowardly explanation.

candidate_datasets.name: BirdLife DataZone
candidate_datasets.role: common cuckoo ecology and breeding information

candidate_datasets.name: BTO BirdFacts
candidate_datasets.role: public bird breeding and life-history facts

obstacles: Cold nature and cowardice are not standard causal variables.
rationale: The species, brood parasitism and egg number are directly documented in mature public ornithological resources. The observable core is decisively resolvable, although Aristotle's explanation is not.

operationalization: Using identified lionesses with parity and age, model litter size by successive birth and test the exact 5-or-6, 4, 3, 2, 1, 0 sequence.

candidate_datasets.name: Species360 Data Science
candidate_datasets.role: zoo population and reproductive data information

obstacles: Individual parity histories are not broadly open.
Wild and captive litter sizes have different observation biases.
rationale: The numerical trajectory has a clear test, and existing demographic records provide litter-size evidence. Fully open, parity-resolved lioness histories are limited, so only the broad pattern can be assessed.

operationalization: Observe egg laying by hens and geese reared without male contact or stored sperm; any unfertilised egg confirms independent formation.

candidate_datasets.name: FAO DAD-IS
candidate_datasets.role: domestic chicken and goose breed context

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: public index of poultry reproduction studies

obstacles: Prior sperm storage must be excluded in observational records.
rationale: The rival hypotheses are sharply distinguished by controlled husbandry, a standard and extensively documented setting. Existing poultry evidence can resolve the claim without new field collection.

operationalization: Compare egg developmental stage at laying or spawning and fecundity across birds and externally spawning fishes, then test whether fecundity predicts less complete internal development.
obstacles: Completeness of an egg needs a developmental definition.
Aquatic fertilization and phylogeny confound the proposed capacity mechanism.
rationale: Existing comparative data can evaluate the pattern and a fecundity association. They cannot cleanly show that internal capacity is the causal reason rather than one of several correlated reproductive adaptations.

operationalization: Code visible yolk and albumen colour compartments in eggs from sampled bird and fish species; any fish egg with distinct colour compartments refutes the universal.
obstacles: Egg colour is not a standardized trait field.
Microscopic composition differs from visually perceived colour.
rationale: The visible character is straightforward and counterexamples are decisive. Public images and descriptions allow many checks, but not comprehensive all-fish and all-bird coverage.

operationalization: Measure yolk fraction and calibrated yellowness in eggs of aquatic and terrestrial birds and compare habitat groups while controlling diet, body size and phylogeny.
obstacles: Open comparative egg-composition data are sparse.
Diet strongly affects yolk colour.
rationale: The size and colour comparison is measurable, but the needed egg measurements are not joined to broad habitat data. Existing studies can test a limited species sample with substantial confounding.

operationalization: Use video or direct records of normal hen oviposition to code whether the blunt or pointed pole emerges first and estimate the proportion blunt-end-first.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: public index of poultry oviposition studies

obstacles: Raw oviposition-orientation video datasets may not be archived.
Rare abnormal orientations should be separated from the typical claim.
rationale: Egg orientation at laying is explicit and requires only standard observations already reported in poultry science. Even literature-level records can decisively confirm or refute the typical orientation.

operationalization: Measure shell hardness at emergence and over minutes after laying under controlled temperature and humidity, testing whether cooling and water loss explain any change.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: public index of eggshell formation and mechanical studies

obstacles: Public time-resolved shell-hardness datasets are scarce.
Shell mineralization largely occurs before laying, requiring a precise hardness endpoint.
rationale: The physical prediction is direct and standard mechanical methods can discriminate it. Existing published evidence addresses shell formation, but reusable immediate post-laying time series are limited.

operationalization: Inspect staged Mustelus embryos for uterine attachment, umbilical connection and yolk depletion; persistence of the connection after yolk use confirms the claim.
obstacles: Detailed images are dispersed through species studies.
Not all smooth-hound species use identical maternal provisioning.
rationale: Placental connections in smooth-hound sharks are established, observable reproductive traits. Existing species records and studies can directly resolve the scoped assertion.

operationalization: Estimate egg-to-hatch survival and fecundity across oviparous fishes and test whether species with greater pre-hatching loss produce more eggs, controlling body size and life history.
obstacles: Egg mortality is difficult to estimate and strongly environment-dependent.
Correlation cannot establish compensatory natural purpose.
rationale: High mortality and fecundity are measurable with existing fish data for some species. The final-cause interpretation is not discriminated by the correlation, and mortality coverage is uneven.

operationalization: Map erythrinus and channa to candidate serranids, then code sexual systems across fishes; any additional hermaphroditic or unisexual fish refutes the exception list.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish sexual systems and reproductive biology

obstacles: Ancient fish names have uncertain mappings.
The claim conflates gonadal anatomy, separate sexes and absence of males.
rationale: Modern fish reproductive databases document diverse sexual systems and make the universal exception list testable. Ambiguous names prevent a completely faithful resolution of the two alleged exceptions.

operationalization: Compare documented fertilization routes and reproductive anatomy in fishes, testing whether swallowed sperm can reach and fertilize oocytes versus external spawning or genital transfer.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish reproductive modes and spawning biology

obstacles: A few unusual internal fertilizers require separate treatment.
rationale: Digestive and reproductive tracts and fish fertilization modes are directly documented. Existing anatomy and reproductive data cleanly discriminate swallowing from established fertilization routes.

operationalization: Examine sexed hyena specimens and images for external genital anatomy, coding one versus both genital systems and the presence of a female-like perineal feature.
obstacles: External similarity does not itself identify internal reproductive sex.
rationale: Hyena genital anatomy is a well-described, directly observable character. Public anatomical accounts can decisively resolve both the absence of dual genital systems and the unusual female morphology.

operationalization: Sequentially mate hens with genetically distinguishable cocks, genotype embryos from already developing follicles, and test whether later paternity or phenotype replaces earlier paternity before albumen separation.
obstacles: Public datasets rarely preserve exact mating sequence and follicle stage.
Sperm storage and multiple paternity must be distinguished from changing an embryo's nature.
rationale: Genotyping provides a decisive experimental criterion, but an existing open dataset matching the precise timing and already-impregnated condition is not evident. A faithful test likely needs a new controlled breeding study.

operationalization: For holometabolous insects, code the stage after the larva for immobility and hardened outer covering, and identify the adult emerging from that pupal stage.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: public observations and images of insect life stages

obstacles: The statement applies only to insects with complete metamorphosis, not all insects.
rationale: Pupation is a standard, richly documented developmental transition in the named groups. Existing observations directly confirm or refute the described immobile, hardened stage.

operationalization: Use life-cycle, oviposition and genetic records for wool moths and aquatic insects to test whether larvae arise without parents or from eggs laid by adults.

candidate_datasets.name: iNaturalist
candidate_datasets.role: observations of adult and immature insect stages

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: DNA barcodes linking immature insects to species

obstacles: Occurrence data alone do not record unseen egg deposition.
rationale: The spontaneous-generation hypothesis makes clear predictions contradicted or supported by observed life cycles and parentage. Existing life-history and barcode data can resolve the representative cases without collecting new data.

operationalization: Determine the maternal caste and ploidy of drone offspring and test whether workers, rather than queens, regularly lay the unfertilised eggs producing drones.
obstacles: Workers can lay drones mainly under queenless conditions, so frequency and context matter.
rationale: Worker-laid haploid drones and their conditions are directly observable through colony and genetic data. Existing bee biology can resolve the factual core, while the plant-like both-sexes description is only analogical.

operationalization: Use pedigrees or genotypes to test whether the queen produces female workers and future queens.
obstacles: The ancient king must be correctly mapped to the queen caste.
rationale: After the explicit historical mapping, parentage and caste development are standard honey-bee biology. Public genetic and natural-history data decisively resolve the claim.

operationalization: Join colony-level weather, honey yield, drone brood and worker brood time series and test whether dry fine periods predict more honey and drones while rainy periods predict more workers.

candidate_datasets.name: COLOSS B-RAP
candidate_datasets.role: honey-bee research association and colony monitoring protocols

candidate_datasets.name: NASA POWER
candidate_datasets.role: public weather data for colony locations

obstacles: Open colony records rarely contain both caste-specific brood and honey.
Season and forage availability confound rainfall effects.
rationale: The predictions are measurable and weather data are abundant, but linked caste-brood colony data are limited. Existing monitoring can test restricted populations with substantial seasonal confounding.

operationalization: No scientific dataset can determine the normative rule that observation ought to receive precedence over theory.
obstacles: The claim prescribes epistemic practice rather than predicting an observation.
rationale: This is a methodological maxim. It has no empirical decision criterion independent of adopting a philosophy of science.

operationalization: Map testaceans to shelled molluscs and comparable attached shelled invertebrates, classify species as terrestrial or marine, and compare taxonomic richness.

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS: World Register of Marine Species

obstacles: Testacean boundaries include several nonhomologous modern groups.
Recorded richness is affected by taxonomic effort.
rationale: Global public taxonomic databases provide environment and richness information at the needed scale. Alternative mappings can be reported, and the broad land-sea contrast is directly resolvable.

operationalization: Classify mollusc, cephalopod and crustacean occurrences by lake, fresh-brackish, estuary and river-mouth habitats and compare richness and frequency.

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS: World Register of Marine Species

obstacles: Salinity and waterbody type are absent from many records.
Sampling effort differs sharply among habitats.
rationale: Large open occurrence systems contain extensive records for all named groups. Habitat metadata and sampling bias need care, but the asserted near-absence and estuarine concentration are testable now.

operationalization: Use eel reproductive observations, larval genetics and life cycles to test whether eels have parents and develop from fertilised eggs rather than earth-derived matter.

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: DNA barcodes connecting eel larvae and adults

obstacles: The mullet and other river fishes are not taxonomically identified.
Natural eel spawning is difficult to observe directly.
rationale: The principal eel assertion has clear genetic and developmental alternatives and extensive modern evidence. Unidentified additional fishes reduce scope coverage but do not prevent resolving the central spontaneous-generation claim.

operationalization: Identify larvae or recruits on boats genetically and compare their life cycles with adult reproduction, testing whether settlement follows dispersal from parents rather than generation from mud.

candidate_datasets.name: WoRMS: World Register of Marine Species
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomy of fouling molluscs and barnacles

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: DNA barcodes for larvae and adults

obstacles: Testaceans map to several modern phyla.
Settlement observations alone can miss microscopic propagules.
rationale: Modern life-cycle and genetic data distinguish spontaneous origin from larval settlement. Existing public resources can resolve representative and broad group claims despite ancient category ambiguity.

operationalization: In litters with sexed fetuses, define uterine compartments and estimate how often opposite-sex twins share the same compartment across mammals and live-bearing fishes.

candidate_datasets.name: Open Science Framework
candidate_datasets.role: public repository potentially hosting reproductive imaging datasets

obstacles: Same part of the uterus is anatomically ambiguous across taxa.
Fetal position and sex are rarely jointly available in open data.
rationale: The co-location frequency is measurable after defining uterine units, but suitable cross-taxon dissection or imaging datasets are sparse. Existing studies support only restricted species-level tests.

operationalization: Code testes presence and production of male and female offspring across fishes and snakes; species with testes refute the anatomical universal, while sex ratios test whether offspring sexes occur.
obstacles: Aristotle may mean externally visible testes rather than gonads.
Not every species has sex-ratio data.
rationale: Gonadal anatomy and offspring sex are standard observations in both groups. Existing anatomy and reproductive sources readily test the factual premise, with interpretation needed for the ancient anatomical term.

operationalization: The stipulative definition of male by concoction and a form-bearing principle has no independent measurable criterion.
obstacles: Concoction and principle of form are not operational biological entities.
The claim is primarily definitional.
rationale: Modern gamete production could test a replacement proposition, but not this definition as stated. No dataset can decide the metaphysical form-bearing component.

operationalization: Define heat as core body temperature or sex-specific metabolic heat production and compare males and females within species using paired conditions.

candidate_datasets.name: Movebank
candidate_datasets.role: animal-borne sensor datasets that may include temperature

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: public repository of comparative physiology datasets

obstacles: Intrinsic heat is ambiguous.
Sex-specific temperature data are sparse and condition-dependent.
rationale: Modern physiological proxies permit direct within-species comparisons, but no broad harmonized dataset represents all animals. Existing sensor and physiology datasets can resolve selected taxa only.

operationalization: Use developmental temperature and molecular sex-determination data to test whether reduced embryonic heat consistently causes female development across animals with separate sexes.

candidate_datasets.name: The Reptile Database
candidate_datasets.role: taxonomic context for temperature-dependent sex determination

obstacles: Male principle and mastering material are not measurable.
Temperature effects differ in direction among taxa and are absent in genetic systems.
rationale: Temperature-dependent sex determination offers an observable partial analogue, but it does not faithfully instantiate Aristotle's mechanism across animals. Existing data can test the heat prediction in subsets and contrast it with genetic alternatives.

operationalization: Model offspring sex against maternal and paternal age with species, parity, cohort and environment controlled, testing for higher female proportions at both age extremes.

candidate_datasets.name: IPUMS International
candidate_datasets.role: harmonized census microdata with parent and child demographics

obstacles: Human census links do not always identify both biological parents.
Comparable animal parent-age datasets are scattered.
rationale: The sex-ratio prediction is clear and large demographic records can test humans. Existing data do not provide equivalent broad animal coverage and observational confounding remains.

operationalization: Link precisely timed conceptions to local wind direction and offspring sex, then compare male proportions for northerly versus southerly winds with season and temperature controlled.

candidate_datasets.name: ERA5
candidate_datasets.role: hourly historical wind direction and weather

obstacles: Public birth records rarely reveal conception time precisely enough to assign wind.
Season, geography and temperature are strong confounders.
rationale: Weather data exist, but the necessary conception-time linkage for humans or domestic animals is not publicly available at adequate precision and scale. A faithful analysis would require newly assembled reproductive records.

operationalization: Convert menstrual onsets to lunar phase and test enrichment during waning phases, then separately test whether temperature or humidity mediates any pattern.

candidate_datasets.name: Clue Research Dataset
candidate_datasets.role: large-scale menstrual-cycle research data access information

obstacles: App users are nonrandom.
The causal cold-and-moist explanation needs location-linked records.
rationale: Large cycle datasets can decisively assess the lunar timing prediction. Location and weather linkage may be incomplete, so the causal explanation is less fully resolved than the central pattern.

operationalization: Using multigenerational pedigrees with standardized facial or morphological traits, compare child-parent, child-grandparent and child-unrelated similarity distributions.

candidate_datasets.name: UK Biobank
candidate_datasets.role: large-scale genetic, imaging and phenotype resource

obstacles: Access is controlled rather than openly downloadable.
Resemblance depends strongly on selected traits and shared environment.
rationale: Kinship and phenotype data can quantify graded resemblance, but public-access multigenerational morphology is limited and the result depends on trait choice. Existing cohorts support a substantial but not scope-complete test.

operationalization: Treat movements as inherited genetic effects and test whether offspring phenotypes not resembling a parent preferentially resemble that parent's ancestors rather than unrelated people.

candidate_datasets.name: UK Biobank
candidate_datasets.role: genetic and phenotype data for modern inheritance models

obstacles: Semen movements and resolution are not observable entities.
A modern genetic proxy changes the stated mechanism.
rationale: Multigenerational resemblance is testable, but Aristotle's serial transformation mechanism has no direct modern variable. Existing family data can address only a proxy consequence, not discriminate the mechanism.

operationalization: Define monstrosity as a major congenital anomaly and compare per-offspring prevalence among singleton-bearing, multiparous and bird species, with a separate estimate for domestic fowl.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: public index of veterinary and avian congenital-anomaly reports

obstacles: Anomaly ascertainment differs radically among humans, livestock and birds.
Per-litter and per-offspring risk must be separated.
No harmonized all-animal anomaly registry exists.
rationale: A modern anomaly definition makes the prediction measurable, and some surveillance data exist. Cross-taxon detection bias and fragmented veterinary records prevent a clean animal-wide ranking.
